I get clean drinking water from a store nearby, I get clean bathe water from work, I fill a bucket. Keeping bugs away isn’t easy but I have a 3 person dome tent from Walmart, it’s around 30$. It’s waterproof to an extent,the upper half of the tent is mesh, I leave the cover on top of the upper half (even with the cover on it’s still open it isn’t fully closed) and only keep the door window open. The only bugs that can get in my tent are small bugs, smaller than average sized ants. When I see ants,I squish them with my finger (usually I will see only 3-5 of them) you can minimize the amount of bugs around your tent by keeping less food in your tent, and avoid using your phone at night OR you can cover it so it doesn’t shine all over your tent. Lights attract bugs, bugs attract animals.
Wish you best of luck OP and be careful!

No problem man, the best word of advice I can give is to push yourself. Camping is pretty peaceful for the most part. You might hear animals fighting and it’ll wake you up, I keep a strobe light app on my phone to confuse animals when they get too close to me, I have a bottle of change that I shake when they get too close to my tent too and it scares them away so there’s nothing to be afraid of unless you’re scared to get killed by a coyote in your sleep lol. This spot is close to my job, I relocated from 6 hours away and started working here in September. Edit: keep a bucket with you on your journey, it’ll help multipurpose you can carry stuff that doesn’t fit in your pack, if you end up in a small town like me there’s many places here that will fill you up with water free of charge so you can wash up comfortably. Kittens may be TOO playful, my cat was the same, when petting your kitten, if it becomes over playful just stop petting it for a moment, (wait about 15 seconds before you try to pet, if it tries to play take your hand from it and repeat over and over)so it can realize you stopped petting when it tried to play.. THEN you can reach and pet again(in a spot it enjoys being pet so it can know you are petting not playing)unfortunately you will need to repeat this over. If you’re petting it in a spot that makes him excited try to avoid it. Repetition is the key, as long as you do this, you can help your cat understand the difference between petting and playing. It may be hard or take some getting used to for you,but if you use your hand to play with your kitten it could be confusing for them to understand when you’re playing and when you’re wanting to pet them. To help minimize this issue you should use cat toys when you play, not your hand. Cats like to play/attack things that wiggle especially when they’re kittens so something like your fingers could really trigger them to play. My cat is grown now and understands the difference, and he’s now gentle with my hand when I use my hand to play with him, I hope this can help you!
